titles.title: HalfLife1
titles.engine_and_build:
WON Half-Life 1.1.0.8 (version.txt: Half-Life / 71176 / 1.1.0.8 / 9/24/2001), GoldSrc protocol 45. Confirmed.
- hl.exe: the 942,080 B WON launcher (md5 77cce9925d2a039ae38b679b1225e944, linked 2001-09-11). It owns the display mode.
- hw.dll: 1,175,552 B, md5 374a87fd6175a6a9541656bc959bc822, linked 2001-09-21 (hardware renderer).
- sw.dll: 1,056,768 B, md5 8dca902ec1e31441adf5fde45c90b378, linked 2001-09-15 (software renderer).

NEW (not in the survey): hl.exe picks the renderer at 0x423c4c-0x423cd8. It reads the registry EngineType, then -d3d sets 3, -gl/-opengl sets 2, and -soft/-software sets 1. So in THIS engine EngineType 1 = software, 2 = OpenGL, 3 = D3D.

There are five launchers:
- Half-Life, Team Fortress Classic and Deathmatch Classic work.
- Opposing Force and Blue Shift are broken for non-refresh reasons (KNOWN-BROKEN-bshift-and-gearbox.txt).
titles.on_boxes:
Deployed at C:\Games\HalfLife1 on .123, .145, .195, .240 and .124 (DIRLIST 00:31).
- Every library file is present at library size.
- Extra files are only hl.dat, a screenshot bmp on .123, and .124's hand-placed DMCTEST/TFCTEST/LANCHECK.BAT. All three use -gl and none sets a refresh.
- There is no game-local opengl32, 3dfxgl or glide DLL on any box.

.243: not deployed. Its share log mirror (N5R5L9-agent.log) repeats 'SKIP HalfLife1 - needs 952 MB + 150 MB kept free, only 196 MB free'. I did not contact .243.

Every box launches 'start "" hl.exe -nosierra -full -gl -w %FR_W43% -h %FR_H43% -toconsole [-game mod]'. That is OpenGL with EngineGLDriver=Default: drvmap.txt reads 'Default Default' and this tree ships no gldrv\3dfxgl.dll. So the system opengl32 hands off to each box's ICD:
- .123: ATI Radeon HD 3850 AGP, 8.970.100.0.
- .240: CORRECTED. The adapter attached to the desktop is a Radeon X1600 Series (1002:71C0), 8.593.100.0 (HWPROFILE 00:34). The X800 and 9800 XT entries are stale class keys; docs/fleet-inventory.md (1 day old) still says X800.
- .195: AMD Radeon HD 5450, Win7, 15.200.1062.1004.
- .145: NVIDIA GeForce 8400GS, 6.14.13.4052. An Intel HD adapter is present but not attached.
- .124: our MesaFX retroicd.dll (OpenGLDrivers\3dfx\DLL=retroicd.dll, re-read 00:55) over OUR h5 glide3x.dll (system32, 1,025,320 B, md5 38a891e81ea58379a0c22be6d7c0d6fb, RETRO3DFX_SLIAA_GUARD/AA_TRACE markers) on vcr-kmd. AmigaMerlin's Glide is parked as glide3x_am31.dll.

EngineDLL=hw.dll on all five boxes.
titles.resolution_per_box:
The launchers use FR_W43 x FR_H43 because the WON engine is 4:3-only. Given 16:9 it falls to 400x300, as measured on .240 per the launcher comment.
- .123, .145, .195, .240: 1280x960 (GAMERES four_three; unchanged on re-read at 00:55).
- .124: 1280x960 (4:3 HP P1120). retrogl.log has every HalfLife1\hl.exe context at 1280x960 (14 processes, 15 context opens). The hand-placed LANCHECK.BAT passes -w 1280 -h 960 explicitly, so the log corroborates the target but does not prove the staged-launcher path.
- .240 caveat: in its 00:10 state (no EDID, no rates, persisted 1024x768) FLEETRES would assume a 4:3 tube and pick 1024x768. At 00:31 and 00:55 it read the DELL E2313H EDID and a persisted 1920x1080@60. Its live desktop was 640x480 at both reads, which is some game's mode.
- .243: n/a.
titles.refresh_control:
NONE in the engine. Confirmed. I re-ran strings -a -t x (ASCII and UTF-16LE, grep -i for freq|refresh|hz|vsync) on the exact staged binaries. None has '-freq', '-refresh' or a refresh cvar:
- hw.dll: r_norefresh (0xe5624), r_glowshellfreq, timerefresh.
- sw.dll: r_glowshellfreq, timerefresh.
- hl.exe: '%d x %d %d hz' (0xd2874, display only), CRefreshDlg/REFRESH_* (the server browser), 'No VSync Hardware'.

hw.dll and sw.dll import no ChangeDisplaySettings and contain no such name for GetProcAddress.

CORRECTION to 'exactly one mode setter': hl.exe has TWO.
- (a) sub_464070 calls ChangeDisplaySettingsA with DEVMODE dmFields 0x1C0000 and flags 4 (CDS_FULLSCREEN). It is the only CDS call that sets a mode; the other three (0x4240cd, 0x464155, 0x46cf5b) are (NULL,0) restores.
- (b) sub_408690 calls sub_4085c0, which calls IDirectDraw v1 SetDisplayMode(w,h,bpp) at 0x408666. The 640x480x16 launcher mode is set the same way at 0x408614.
- The dispatcher at 0x4641cc uses (b) when the DirectDraw object at 0x4e1a20 exists, and (a) otherwise.
- At 0x40e824 the software renderer (1, fullscreen) and D3D (3) create that object, while OpenGL (2) releases it (sub_408560). So the staged -gl launchers take path (a).
- IDirectDraw v1 SetDisplayMode has no refresh parameter, so no renderer of this build can request a rate.

Only external levers exist:
1. Re-apply the mode with DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY from outside (agent/tools/refreshkeep.c).
2. On .124: the ICD's fxBestRefresh (env FX_GLIDE_REFRESH_RATE / SSTV2_REFRESH_RATE / MESA_FX_REFRESH, else the highest EnumDisplaySettings rate at WxH), plus the h5 Glide's FX_GLIDE_REFRESH.
3. NEW: a driver-level override exists on the ATI XP boxes. '3D_Refresh_Rate_Override_DEF'=0 is present under the adapter's Control\Video\{GUID}\0000 key on .123 and .240 (dumps in evidence-refresh/mechanism/boxes). So 'not verified to exist' is wrong for ATI. What its values mean, and whether it covers OpenGL, is unverified. .145's ForceWare 340.52 key has no equivalent value.
titles.set_today:
Nothing sets a refresh for this title. Confirmed.
- Launchers: they call FLEETRES.BAT, which publishes FR_HZ (the persisted desktop rate: 60 on the LCDs, 85 on .124). No launcher line uses FR_HZ.
- install.reg: it pins HKCU\Software\Valve\Half-Life\Settings to 1024x768x32 and EngineType 1; the key has no refresh field. NEW: EngineType 1 is SOFTWARE in this engine's own renderer switch, not 'hardware/OpenGL' as the comments in install.reg and gameres.h say. That is harmless only because every launcher passes -gl.
- GAMERES rules: gameres.h has no HalfLife1 rule (grep count 0); the shared-key rows are CounterStrike16's. No GoldSrc rule or file carries %FRHZ%, so the FLEETRES/GAMERES byte-identity rule is not involved.
- Desktop refresh raise: it changed nothing. The LCD boxes' agent logs read 'best 60 Hz at 1920x1080, 75 Hz at 1280x960, 60 Hz at the desktop 1920x1080 (panel max 76 Hz); desktop is persisted at 60 Hz'. .124's reads 'best 85 ... persisted at 85 Hz'.
titles.best_per_box:
At 1280x960 (gr_best_hz; the GAMERES re-read at 00:55 matches 00:31). Confirmed.
- .123: 75. DELL P2312H analog, EDID range 56-76 Hz, 30-83 kHz, 170 MHz; 1280x960@75 (about 75 kHz and 130 MHz) fits.
- .145: 75. DELL E2414H analog, same range.
- .195: 60. HP 2511 digital. GAMERES reports only the BEST rate per mode, so 60 is the best rate listed, not necessarily the only one.
- .240: 75. DELL E2313H over DVI, 56-76 Hz. The answer becomes 0 (unknown) if the box falls back to its 00:10 state with no EDID and no rates.
- .124: 85. vcr-kmd's timing table has 1280x960 at 60, 75 and 85 (common/vcr_modes.c lines 42, 43, 88), and the EDID vmax is 160.
- .243: n/a.
titles.expected_today_per_box:
- .123, .145, .240: most likely 60 Hz at 1280x960. NOT measured for this title.
  - Precedents: on .124 (GF2, ForceWare 71.89, 2026-08-25) a same-mode switch with no frequency gave 60 although 100 was stored; .143 (GF6800, 2026-09-26/27) behaved the same way.
  - New corroboration from tonight's agent-log DISPLAYCFG 'Current:' lines (share mirrors): .123 640x480x32 and x16 @60, .145 640x480 @60, .240 640x480 and 1152x864 @60. Each was at a mode where GAMERES lists 75. The log does not say which title or API produced them.
- .195: 60 likely but UNMEASURED, and less certain than the survey says. The HP 2511 EDID has a CEA extension block (byte 126 = 1) and a 50 Hz vertical minimum, so the Win7 driver may list 59 or 50 Hz entries below the 60 GAMERES reports. Where a no-frequency switch lands under WDDM has not been observed.
- .124: 85 Hz REQUESTED; where it lands is unmeasured.
  - retrogl.log: every HalfLife1 context logs 'fxBestRefresh: 1280x960 max 85 Hz (EnumDisplaySettings) -> GR_REFRESH enum 7' and 'grSstWinOpenExt ... ref=7', with glideContext 1875785076.
  - Our h5 Glide then sets the mode itself with IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode(1280,960,32,85,0) (win_mode.c setVideoMode). If that call fails, it silently retries at refresh 0 (the driver default). So the log proves the request, not the rate.
  - The engine's own no-frequency switch runs first, so the CRT re-syncs twice per launch. That is existing behaviour.
titles.gap:
- .123, .145, .240: most likely 60 against 75 available at 1280x960, a 15 Hz gap. Unmeasured.
- .195: none expected, since 60 is the best rate listed. There is an unmeasured risk of a sub-60 landing.
- .124: none if the 85 Hz request lands. Unmeasured.

The engine cannot be told a rate on any renderer. The desktop raise cannot reach it either: XP gives a no-frequency switch the adapter default, even at the same mode.

The premise 'those engines take whatever the desktop is on' (agent/src/gameres.c lines 529-539, the NOTE ON REFRESH in gameres.h, stage-fleetres.py around line 1461, and CLAUDE.md) is contradicted by the 2026-08-25 measurement. Confirmed.
titles.fix:
This title needs the generic external hold. Keep the survey's design, with these corrections.

1. **New FLEETRES variable.** FLEETRES.EXE publishes FR_HZ43, computed EXACTLY as gameres.h computes %HZ43%: rates 50-199, clamped at EDID vmax, 0 when none, preferably at 32 bpp.
   - Do NOT define it as 'empty when FR_EDID=0'. gameres.h does not zero rates when there is no EDID: gr_enum_modes(..., panel.ok ? vmax : 0) just skips the clamp; only gr_raise_desktop_refresh refuses. That definition would make FR_HZ43 and %HZ43% disagree on every no-EDID box. Put the EDID requirement in the launcher test instead.
   - Add 'set FR_HZ43=' to FLEETRES.BAT's reset block, with a fallback of 0, never 60.
   - FLEETRES.BAT and FLEETRES.EXE are identical in every title (md5 23edd351... and bb180f3b...), so this means restaging the whole library through stage-fleetres.py, then running validate-staged-library.py and GAMESYNC on every box.
2. **Stage the helper.** Ship refreshkeep as REFRKEEP.EXE (agent/tools/refreshkeep.exe: console app, subsystem 4.0, imports only KERNEL32/msvcrt/USER32, so it loads on XP and 7).
3. **Gate on the right fact.** FR_GLIDE only means 'VEN_121A appears somewhere in the PCI enum'. It is also 1 on .143, whose V5 5500 is a second adapter behind the GeForce 6800 that renders GL; that is exactly the box where refreshkeep was proven necessary. It is also 1 on any Voodoo 2 pass-through box. Use GlideRender instead: HKLM\Software\RetroAgent GlideRender=1 on .124 (read 00:31), already exposed as FR_UE1DEV=GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice, or add an FR_GLIDERENDER variable. Put this line before each start line, with no parentheses:
   if not "%FR_UE1DEV%"=="GlideDrv.GlideRenderDevice" if "%FR_EDID%"=="1" if not "%FR_HZ43%"=="0" start "" /min "%~dp0REFRKEEP.EXE" %FR_HZ43% hl.exe 14400
4. **Change the resolution line in the generator at the same time.** stage-fleetres.py's HalfLife1 spec still rewrites the launchers to -w %FR_W% -h %FR_H%. The 2026-08-30 FR_W43 correction exists only in the staged .bat files, so regenerating from a pristine launcher would bring back the 400x300 failure.

Expected results:
- .123, .145, .240: 1280x960@75.
- .195: no action if it lands at 60; the helper forces 60 if Win7 picks a lower listed rate.
- .124: skipped by GlideRender; its ICD already asks Glide for 85.

Alternatives:
- Fold the hold into FLEETRES.EXE as a -hold <proc> <hz> mode.
- ATI 3D_Refresh_Rate_Override on .123 and .240. It is a per-box driver setting with unverified semantics, so A/B it first, and it is not a library fix.

Not recommended:
- Code-cave patching sub_464070. It receives no rate, so a patch means adding new code to a 2001 exe.
- Swapping in the Steam-era engine.
titles.fix_risk:
Medium. The survey's risks are confirmed; additions are marked.
- **WM_DISPLAYCHANGE under a live GL context:** shown harmless only for Quake II and UT99 OpenGLDrv on .143's GeForce 6800. Untested for WON GoldSrc, Catalyst 8.970 (.123), Catalyst 8.593 on .240's X1600 (not an X800), ForceWare 340.52 (.145) and Win7/WDDM (.195).
- **Second switch:** every mode set the engine does is followed within about 1 s by a second one. An LCD shows that as a re-sync blink, and it repeats after each alt-tab return.
- **LCD benefit unproven:** these are 60 Hz-native panels that accept 75 Hz, and the scaler may frame-convert, so the gain has to be seen.
- **ADDED - no mode filter:** refreshkeep applies the explicit rate at WHATEVER mode is current, as long as the driver lists that rate there. That is safe here because FR_HZ43 is EDID-clamped and the driver lists are range-filtered, but consider restricting it to FR_W43 x FR_H43.
- **Matches Counter-Strike too:** watching hl.exe also catches CS. Harmless, because 75 is not listed at 1920x1080.
- **Glide boxes:** the helper must never run where Glide owns the display. The gate above prevents that and keeps the CRT pacing rule intact on .124.
- **New binary:** one more binary in the tree for GAMESYNC and the validator.
- **ADDED - no record:** refreshkeep prints only to its own minimized console, which disappears on exit. Nothing is recorded unless its output is redirected.
titles.verify_on_hw:
**.123, .145, .195, .240** - after the 1080p workflow releases their screens:
1. Run the staged Half-Life.bat, Team Fortress Classic.bat or Deathmatch Classic.bat.
   - CORRECTION: the staged TFC/DMC launchers do NOT reach a map on their own. They have no +map; only .124's hand-placed TFCTEST/DMCTEST add one. They stop at the engine console, which is already fullscreen at the target mode, and that is enough.
2. While it runs, send DISPLAYCFG get (EnumDisplaySettings ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS, the method used in the 2026-08-25 measurement). Expect 1280x960x32 and today's rate.
3. Cross-check the monitor OSD.
4. On .145, confirm the answer comes from the GeForce: CLAUDE.md records DISPLAYCFG get once reading the inactive Intel HD there. It read 1920x1080@60 at 00:55, but compare with WINLIST.
5. After the fix, expect 75 on .123/.145/.240 and 60 on .195. To see refreshkeep's 't=..s 1280x960x32 60Hz -> 75Hz: rc=0' line, redirect its output to a file (e.g. %TEMP%\refrkeep-hl.log); as proposed it only prints to a transient console.

**.124:**
1. DOWNLOAD C:\retrogl.log and read the newest HalfLife1 block: max 85 Hz, enum 7, non-zero glideContext.
2. Send DISPLAYCFG get during play. It IS informative here, because Glide's mode set is a DirectDraw mode change: 85 means the request landed, and anything else means Glide's silent refresh-0 fallback fired.
3. Confirm the scan-out with the P1120 OSD or a vcrctl register read (pixclk / (htotal*vtotal)).
- FX_GLIDE_TRACE=1 (C:\vcr\glidelab\glidetrace.log) records the requested refresh but not the fallback.
- Coordinate with the V5 6000 lane and add no extra mode switches.
titles.verifier_notes:
**Confirmed (could not refute):**
- Binaries, sizes, md5s and link dates.
- No refresh switch or cvar in hl.exe, hw.dll or sw.dll, re-run case-insensitively in ASCII and UTF-16.
- sub_464070 sets dmFields 0x1C0000 and calls CDS(..., CDS_FULLSCREEN) with no DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY.
- The hz column is display-only (table 0x4e6e34, stride 300, hz at +0x24).
- hw.dll and sw.dll import no ChangeDisplaySettings.
- Deployment and tree identity on the five boxes; the .243 SKIP line in its log mirror.
- GAMERES best rates (re-read 00:55); no HalfLife1 rule; no shared cfg, so no FLEETRES/GAMERES byte fight; the desktop raise is a no-op.
- retrogl.log counts: 14 processes, 15 opens, all ref=7.
- The FINDINGS 2026-08-25 and .143 precedents.
- _priority.txt order (CounterStrike16 line 3, HalfLife1 line 8), and the per-title gs_merge_reg then gameres_apply_title order in gamesync.c 5520-5533. So on every full sync HalfLife1's install.reg re-pins the shared key after CS's rows have written it.

**Refuted or corrected:**
1. hl.exe has a second mode setter, IDirectDraw v1, used by the software and D3D renderers. It has no refresh parameter either, so the conclusion stands.
2. WON EngineType is 1 = software, 2 = OpenGL, 3 = D3D. .124's EngineType=2 already means OpenGL, so there is nothing for -gl to 'override'. The 'EngineType 1 = hardware/OpenGL' comments in install.reg and gameres.h are wrong for this engine and harmless only because of -gl.
3. .240 renders on a Radeon X1600, not an X800.
4. 'Driver override not verified to exist' is wrong for ATI: 3D_Refresh_Rate_Override_DEF is present on .123 and .240.
5. FR_GLIDE is the wrong gate: it means silicon is present, not that Glide renders. Use GlideRender.
6. The fix's 'gr_best_hz rule' and 'empty when FR_EDID=0' contradict each other. The orchestrator's 'no EDID = no refresh claim (gameres.h rule)' holds only for the desktop raise; %HZ%/%HZ43% carry the unclamped driver maximum when there is no EDID.
7. .124's 85 Hz is a logged request, and our h5 Glide can silently fall back to the driver-default refresh.
8. .195 may list sub-60 rates (CEA extension, vmin 50).
9. The staged TFC/DMC launchers do not reach a map.
10. The generator's HalfLife1 spec is stale: it writes FR_W where the staged launchers use FR_W43.

**Evidence** (all under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-refresh/goldsrc-review/):
- won_hl_exe_second_modesetter.disasm.txt
- strings-refresh-grep.txt, imports.txt, md5.txt, edid-decode.txt
- live/reprobe-{123,124,145,195,240}.json, live/edid-*.json, live/124-glide3x.dll
- tools/sweep.py, tools/reprobe.py

The ATI registry dumps are in .claude/evidence-refresh/mechanism/boxes/.

Boxes were touched read-only only: GAMERES, DISPLAYCFG get, DIRLIST, REGREAD, and a DOWNLOAD of .124's glide3x.dll. .243 and .249 were not contacted.

titles.title: CounterStrike16
titles.engine_and_build:
Counter-Strike 1.6, ZCP 'No-Steam V42' build 4554, protocol 48 (per the launcher and install.reg comments), with RevEmu (rev.ini, revSrvBrowser.dll). Confirmed.
- hl.exe: 86,077 B, md5 2098ccf443433129b556c2849fe99e26, linked 2008-10-22. A loader only: it imports WSOCK32/KERNEL32/USER32/ADVAPI32, with no DDRAW and no ChangeDisplaySettings.
- hw.dll: 1,840,440 B, md5 4903e8e80f2a00d3ab2886f0f209a6d6, linked 2009-06-15, base 0x1d00000. RTTI names .?AVCVideoMode_Common@@, .?AVCVideoMode_OpenGL@@ and .?AVCVideoMode_Direct3DFullScreen@@.
- sw.dll: 1,672,504 B, md5 05c1e82726cd5ab6518864f77947527c. Software renderer; carries no '-freq'.

The tree's second shortcut, 'Play Half-Life Deathmatch.bat', runs the same engine with -game valve against the fleet server.
titles.on_boxes:
Deployed at C:\Games\CounterStrike16 on .123, .145, .195, .240 and .124 (DIRLIST 00:31).
- Every library file is present at library size, and there is no game-local GL or Glide DLL.
- Extra files are only qconsole.log (.195, .124), plus on .124 V56KBENCH.BAT, LANCHECK.BAT and 13 old Steam_*.mdmp crash dumps.

.243: gated. Its share log mirror reads 'GATED CounterStrike16 - cpu_mhz: CPU too slow (have 165 MHz, needs 233) [rule]'.

Both launchers run 'start "" hl.exe -game cstrike|valve -full -gl -w %FR_W% -h %FR_H%'; the Deathmatch one adds +connect 192.168.1.132:27020. Both set MESA_FORCE_SSE=1, which has no effect on refresh.

The renderer choice, disassembled at 0x1dc7a80, checks -d3d first, then -gl, then the registry value EngineD3D. So -gl beats the stale EngineD3D=1 on .145 and .240. Confirmed.

The tree ships gldrv\3dfxgl.dll (a 3dfx MiniGL), but EngineGLDriver=Default on all five boxes (GAMERES pins it), so GL goes to the system ICD. The per-box ICDs are the same as for HalfLife1, with two notes:
- .240 is a Radeon X1600 (1002:71C0), not an X800.
- .124 runs retroicd.dll over our h5 glide3x.dll on vcr-kmd.
titles.resolution_per_box:
The launchers use FR_W x FR_H.
- .123, .145, .195, .240: 1920x1080, equal to the persisted desktop. HKCU ScreenWidth/Height read 1920x1080 on all four.
- .240 caveat: its 00:10 no-EDID state would give 1024x768.
- .124: 1280x960, the largest 4:3 mode under its 1280x1024 desktop on a 4:3 tube. retrogl.log shows all 9 CS contexts at 1280x960. LANCHECK.BAT passes 1280x960 explicitly, and V56KBENCH.BAT (640x480) does not appear in the current log.
- .243: n/a.

The -w/-h override is CONFIRMED. CVideoMode_Common::Init reads ScreenWidth/Height/BPP, then -width/-w and -height/-h (strings 0x1e8ca38, 0x1e8ca40, 0x1e8ca44, 0x1e8ca4c; code 0x1dc694d-0x1dc69f1). This refutes both install.reg files, which say CS 'ignores -w/-h'. That observation fits the repack Counter-Strike.exe not forwarding arguments (FINDINGS 2026-08-03).

Small correction: the match against the enumerated mode list compares width and height only (12-byte entries). It takes an exact match, else the last entry with the same width, else mode 0.
titles.set_today:
-freq is passed nowhere. Confirmed. FLEETRES.BAT publishes FR_HZ, and nothing uses it.

The GAMERES rows for this title write only the shared HKCU Valve\Settings key:
- ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight = %W%/%H%
- ScreenBPP 32, ScreenWindowed 0
- EngineModeW/EngineModeH = %W%/%H%, EngineModeBPP 32, EngineModeWindowed 0
- EngineType 1, EngineGLDriver Default

None of these is a refresh. No GoldSrc rule uses %FRHZ%, so no shared-cfg byte identity is involved.

The desktop raise has nothing to raise: 1920x1080@60 and 1280x1024@85 are already the best.

This tree's install.reg pins 800x600x32 in the same key. Ordering fact: in a full GAMESYNC, CounterStrike16 (priority line 3) is merged and its rows applied BEFORE HalfLife1 (line 8), whose install.reg then re-pins 1024x768. The key is only a fallback, because -w/-h wins.
titles.best_per_box:
At 1920x1080:
- .123: 60. CORRECTED wording: it is not that 'only the 4:3 modes reach 75'. On .123 every listed mode from 800x600 to 1680x1050 is @75 (720x480 is @60). 1920x1080 stops at 60 because 75 Hz there would exceed the EDID range (83 kHz, 170 MHz).
- .145: 60.
- .195: 60. This is the best rate listed; lower entries are possible (see expected_today).
- .240: 60. The answer would be 0 (unknown) in the 00:10 state.
- .124: 85 at 1280x960 (vcr-kmd lists 60/75/85; EDID vmax 160).
- .243: n/a.
titles.expected_today_per_box:
- .123, .145, .240: 60 Hz at 1920x1080. Not measured for CS, but bounded: 60 is the only rate those EDID ranges admit at 1080p (vmin 56, no extension blocks, max pixel clock 170 MHz). Consistent with tonight's agent-log readings of 1920x1080x16 @60 on .123, .145 and .240.
- .195: 60 likely, but UNMEASURED. The HP 2511 EDID has a CEA extension (byte 126 = 1) and vmin 50, so 59 or 50 Hz 1080p entries may exist below the 60 GAMERES reports. Where a no-frequency switch lands on Win7/WDDM has not been observed.
- .124: 85 Hz REQUESTED; where it lands is unmeasured. retrogl.log has 9 CS contexts, each logging 'fxBestRefresh: 1280x960 max 85 Hz ... enum 7' and 'grSstWinOpenExt ... ref=7', glideContext 1875785076, with no ICD retry. Our h5 Glide silently retries at refresh 0 if IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode(...,85) fails, so the log proves the request, not the rate.
titles.gap:
- None expected on .123, .145 and .240: 60 is the maximum at 1080p.
- .124: none if the Glide request lands.
- .195: unmeasured, with a possible sub-60 landing.

The latent gap is confirmed: wherever FR_W x FR_H differs from the desktop on a non-Glide box, the no-frequency switch gets the adapter default, although the engine could take -freq.

But the survey's example .143 would NOT be fixed by its own proposal. .143 has no readable EDID (per CLAUDE.md), so FR_HZW is empty (or 0) there by design. An EDID-readable CRT box such as .133 would benefit.

The 'GoldSrc has no refresh setting' docs are right for WON 1.1.0.8 and wrong for build 4554. Confirmed, at: the NOTE ON REFRESH in gameres.h, gameres.c line 534, stage-fleetres.py line 1461, the refreshkeep.c header, retro-3dfx FINDINGS line 3110 and its 2026-08-25 entry, and CLAUDE.md.
titles.fix:
No change is needed for the connected boxes. The hardening is sound with these corrections.

1. **Compute FR_HZW at the engine's exact mode.** It must be the best rate at exactly FR_W x FR_H x 32 bpp: 32 is the engine's ScreenBPP, which GAMERES pins.
